strings.name: Bob Dylan
strings.summary: Bob Dylan brought folk, blues and rock into a changing songwriting practice, combining social observation, personal experience and poetic imagery. Emerging from New York’s folk scene, he moved into electric music and repeatedly changed styles. His work reached musicians and literary readers alike. Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016, he continued recording and touring in later life.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to 2026-11-11. This is not a complete catalogue of works or appearances; later plans are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: Combined folk, rock and poetic writing, expanded the literary possibilities of song, and received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Expanding the literary scope of song
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Used narrative, imagery and social observation in popular lyrics, receiving the Nobel literature prize and a Pulitzer Special Citation.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Continual artistic change
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Moved from folk to electric rock and kept exploring vocal, recording and touring approaches.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Continued European touring
strings.timeline.event-1.text: His official site records a performance at Vienna’s Wiener Stadthalle and its setlist.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Released Rough and Rowdy Ways
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Issued an album of new original songs, continuing his later recording career.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Received the Nobel literature prize
strings.timeline.event-3.text: The Swedish Academy recognized his poetic innovation within American song.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Received a Pulitzer Special Citation
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Honored for his lasting influence on popular music and American culture.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Released Time Out of Mind
strings.timeline.event-5.text: The album became a major landmark in his later career.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Released Blood on the Tracks
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Personal storytelling shaped one of his signature albums.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Turned toward electric rock
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Released Highway 61 Revisited as electric performances divided folk audiences.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Released The Freewheelin’ Bob Dylan
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Original songs established his place in the folk revival.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Released his debut album
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Columbia issued Bob Dylan, mixing traditional material and original songs.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Moved to New York
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Joined the Greenwich Village folk scene and signed with Columbia.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Entered university
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Attended the University of Minnesota before leaving to develop a music career.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Duluth
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born Robert Allen Zimmerman; grew up in Minnesota.
